summary.text: Andy Hopper is a Republican state representative from Texas House District 64 who has represented the district since 2025 and is seeking re-election in the November 3, 2026 general election. A software engineer, he is also a small farmer and a chief warrant officer in the Texas State Guard.

paragraphs.text: Andy Hopper was born in Kansas City, Missouri, and earned a bachelor's degree from Ohio University in 1997 and a graduate degree from the University of North Texas in 2000.

His career experience includes working as a software engineer, owner of a software consulting firm, and small farmer, as a chief warrant officer in the Texas State Guard, and as an adjunct professor at the University of North Texas.
Ballotpedia lists his affiliations as including the Decatur Rotary, Wise County Republican Party, and co-founder of Wise County Conservatives and the Trinity Conservative Coalition.
Hopper took office on January 14, 2025, succeeding Lynn Stucky.
He advanced from the Republican primary on March 3, 2026, and faces Democrat Julie Evans in the general election.
In a Ballotpedia survey, he said Texans should decide what is best for Texas rather than federal officials and said he would vote to ensure that Republicans lead House committees.
